newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK CHIEF SEES FEWER BANKS BY END OF 1997.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK CHIEF SEES FEWER BANKS BY END OF 1997.

text.p: The govenor of Lithuania's central bank, Reinoldijus Sharkinas, said on Thursday that he was sure there would be fewer banks operating in the country by the end of the year.
"I am sure that we will finish 1997 with a lower number of banks," Sharkinas told a news conference.
"I think that there will appear at least one or two European level banks which will be capable of competing with foreign banks," Sharkinas said.
Lithuania currently has 12 commercial banks, three of which are state-run.
The sector seems to have recovered from a crisis which broke in late 1995 with the surprise closure of two of the country's largest banks.
Most banks have reported higher profits for 1996 than for 1995.
Sharkinas said that there was a market for smaller banks but added that some of them would have to boost their share capital this year or merge with larger banks.
Sector analysts say that smaller banks will have difficulty scrambling to meet tighter central bank requirements.
